paragraphs: Many young people today cannot reach important life goals easily. Buying a house or starting a family costs too much money.

House prices and rent are very high. Job pay stays low. Social media also shows rich people who enjoy life. Young adults feel sad and confused about money. Experts say that young people today have less money than their parents.
Young people are learning how to use their money better. They ask for help. Many young people are also protesting to ask politicians for fair prices, better jobs, and a good future.

paragraphs: Younger generations are finding it harder than ever to reach classic adult milestones like buying a home or starting a family. Statistics show over 70% of Gen Z have delayed these major life goals due to sky-high house prices, high rent,

In places like the UK, buying a property now costs up to twelve times the average salary, which makes home ownership feel like a distant dream. On top of that, social media constantly exposes young people to unrealistic standards of wealth, creates unnecessary pressure, and leads to poor financial decisions.

Economic experts point out that Gen Z is projected to be less wealthy than their parents due to high interest rates and inflation. However, rather than giving up, young people are adapting, learning about personal finance, and taking to activism or public protests to demand real political change for their future.

paragraphs: Young adults in Gen Z are struggling to reach traditional life goals like buying a house, getting married, or having children. High house prices, expensive rent, and low salaries mean that young people delay these milestones.

In many countries, buying a home now costs up to ten times an average yearly salary. Social media makes things worse because young people compare themselves to online images of rich people, which causes stress and bad financial choices. Experts say this generation may be less rich than their parents because of inflation and high living costs.

Instead of giving up, many young people are learning how to manage their money better. Many are also joining political protests to fight for lower costs, fair treatment, and a better future for everyone.
